we are trying to understand how the brain is affected by the heart and how we can use this knowledge to improve the treatment of patients who have suffered a cardiac arrest and survived the initial resuscitation.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of the neuron specific enolase (NSE) biomarker in combination with the clinical Glasgow-Pittsburgh Cerebral Performance Category (GPCPC) score is a promising method to assess neurological outcome after cardiac arrest.
the serum levels of NSE are a useful biomarker of brain damage after cardiac arrest.
